name: dev-memory-v1
description: Developer project memory: conventions, decisions, quirks and errors, with queries in the forms agents and people actually use. Paraphrase cases have no word overlap on purpose; lexical retrieval is expected to miss many of them.

memories.content: Use pnpm for every package install; npm and yarn lockfiles are rejected in CI
We chose SQLx over Diesel because compile-time checked queries caught 3 production bugs
Integration tests need Postgres running: start it with docker compose up -d db before cargo test
The payments webhook test is flaky on CI because the Stripe sandbox rate-limits; it retries once
Production deploys go through GitHub Actions and need a manual approval from the on-call engineer
UserService.getById returns null for soft-deleted users; use getByIdIncludingDeleted in admin tools
Never commit .env files; local secrets come from 1Password via op run
Kubernetes workloads run in the payments-prod namespace; staging uses payments-stg
Session tokens live in Redis with a 24 hour TTL; logout deletes the key immediately
Database migrations run automatically on deploy via sqlx migrate run; never edit an applied migration
ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:5432 in tests means the Postgres container is not running
The frontend builds with Node 20; Node 18 breaks the Vite plugin for SVG imports
Feature flags are read from LaunchDarkly at startup and cached for 60 seconds
Use structured logging with tracing; println! is blocked by a clippy lint in CI
Public API routes are versioned under /v2; /v1 returns 410 Gone since March 2026
Keep pull requests under 400 changed lines; larger changes need a design note first
All timestamps are stored in UTC; convert to the user's timezone only in the UI
CI caches the cargo target directory keyed by Cargo.lock; clear it after toolchain upgrades
ห้ามใช้ไลบรารีที่ไม่มีไลเซนส์ในโปรเจกต์นี้
ทุกการเปลี่ยนแปลงฐานข้อมูลต้องผ่านการรีวิวจากทีมแบ็กเอนด์
订单服务使用PostgreSQL，因为需要事务支持
缓存层使用Redis，键名以服务名开头
デプロイの前に必ずマイグレーションを実行する
배포 전에 데이터베이스를 백업한다
Authentication uses short-lived JWTs signed with RS256; refresh tokens rotate on every use
The public API rate limit is 100 requests per minute per key; internal services are exempt
The monorepo uses Turborepo; run turbo run test --filter=web to test only the web app
On-call rotates weekly on Mondays; the schedule lives in PagerDuty
User image uploads go to S3 via presigned URLs and are resized by a Lambda
Switching the test runner to Bun might cut CI time by half
